chunks: Interfaces in the signal path and distortion. The question: How do any interfaces in the transmission path impact signal quality and reflections?
What are some interfaces that may introduce distortion?
A high-speed link is a chain of pieces: the chip's package, solder balls, vias, the trace, a coupling capacitor, a connector and maybe a cable, then the same on the far side.
Each hand-off between pieces is an interface where the geometry changes. Every interface can reflect part of the signal and also slow its edges.
Together they can close the eye even when the copper trace itself is fine.
Think of a relay of water pipes. Each joint between pipes of slightly different size makes a little splash back and a little slowdown. One joint is no problem.
A dozen joints in a row can turn a crisp spurt into a smear. The pipes themselves may be perfect. The joints are the interfaces.
Every arrow is an interface.

A typical backplane link crosses 8–12 of them, and at 10+ Gb/s the sum of their parasitics usually sets the return loss and a large share of the bandwidth loss, alongside the copper and dielectric loss of the traces.
Interface: any transition where the structure or impedance changes, such as pad to via or connector to cable.
Return loss: how much of a wave bounces back, in dB ("Reflections and why they matter").
ISI (inter-symbol interference): earlier bits smearing into later ones ("What an eye diagram shows"). Rise time: how long an edge takes to go from low to high.
RSS combination: independent rise-time contributions add as the square root of the sum of squares.
In a 50 ohms line, a 1 nanohenries series inductance adds about 22 picoseconds of rise time, and a 0. 5 picofarads shunt capacitance adds about 27. 5 picoseconds.
A clean 30 picoseconds edge passes both. The new rise time is square root of 30 squared plus 22 squared plus 27. 5 squared about 46 picoseconds.
A few more such interfaces push it past half a bit at 10 Gb/s. That is the whole idea.
"Every interface in the path (package, ball, via, AC cap, connector, cable) is a small impedance discontinuity.
Each reflects part of the edge and also acts as a low-pass filter: 1 nanohenries in a 50 ohms line adds about 22 picoseconds of rise time, 0.
5 picofarads about 27 picoseconds, and they combine in RSS. Spaced discontinuities also resonate, and connectors add crosstalk and mode conversion.
I minimise their number and parasitics, match impedance through them, and check with TDR, S-parameters or an eye diagram."
